bands.1:
The Vantadome glows gold on the dark sea. Forty million Vantafam are watching.

Old Glimmer is stuck in a gold net under the yacht.

"Maxx it out!" cries Maxx. "Tonight I rescue THE BIG ONE!"

You creep up in the dark. BOLT-9 opens a hatch with his old key. Wren leads you to Deck 5.

"This is where I found them," she says. "This is why I ran."

Wren opens every cage.

BOLT-9 plugs into the stream. It needs a password. Zed tries MAXXISGREAT. Wrong.

Wren types SIRNIBBLES. It works. "He has used it since he was nine," she says.

BOLT-9 fills every screen. "Good evening. I rate this show zero out of ten."

He plays all the proof he scanned. The onion script. The squeaky tapes. The one carrot. The cage photos. The Wishlist. The deleted questions. The cage park plans. And Maxx, throwing his own net.

"Is it scared?" ask the comments.

Kaydence, his co-host, does not know her own camera is on. "When he sinks, his fans are mine," she hisses. Her fans hear it.

Then Wren steps into the shot. "Hi, Max. It's me."

"Wrennie?" Maxx has no catchphrase.

Everyone looks at you. "Open the net," you say.

You pull the lever. Old Glimmer rises, shining. Creatures whoosh down the waterslide.

"My finale!" yells Maxx. He jumps on the Gold Rush.

Old Glimmer flicks her tail. Splash! Maxx falls in. His hair goes flat.

You throw him a life ring. "Biggest rescue ever," says Zed. "Live."

"I'm sorry, Wren," says Maxx. There is no onion.

A month later, he helps at a rescue shelter. His badge says MAX. One X. "One chance," says Wren.

"What did the sea say to the Captain?" asks Mo. "Nothing. It just waved!"

"Three out of ten," says BOLT-9. Mo is thrilled.

Old Glimmer glows below. Next to her glows a tiny light. "That's a baby," says Tully.
bands.2:
The Vantadome blazes on the dark sea. Forty million Vantafam are watching, and every screen says, "BIGGEST RESCUE EVER, LIVE!"

Under the yacht, trapped in a gold net, Old Glimmer glows a slow, frightened blue.

"Maxx it out, Vantafam!" cries Maxx. "Tonight, I rescue THE BIG ONE!"

"Stay cray!" adds Kaydence Kray beside him, her helmet camera blinking.

The Soggy Biscuit creeps closer with its lights off.

BOLT-9 opens a hatch with his old key. Wren leads the way down to Deck 5.

"This is where I found them," she says. "This is why I ran."

Inside, the cages go on and on. This time, Wren's hands don't shake.

BOLT-9 plugs his wrist into the stream's control desk. Zed types MAXXISGREAT. Wrong.

Wren types SIRNIBBLES. The screen turns green.

"He hasn't changed it since he was nine," she says.

BOLT-9's face fills every screen. "Good evening. I rate tonight's show zero out of ten. Allow me to improve it."

He plays every piece of proof he ever scanned: the onion script, the squeaky tapes, the one-carrot ledger, the cage photos, the Wishlist, the deleted questions and the cage park plans. Last comes Maxx, throwing his own net.

The hearts stop. The comments flood in: "Is it scared?" "Is that a CAGE?"

"Cut the feed!" screams Kaydence. But her own camera is still on. "When he sinks, his followers are mine," she hisses. Her fans hear every word.

"The Reef Rays are winning!" breathes Tully.

"TULLY!"

Then Wren walks straight into the shot. "Hi, Max," she says. "It's me."

"Wrennie?" For the first time ever, Maxx has no catchphrase.

Everyone looks at you.

"Open the net," you say.

You pull the crane lever. Old Glimmer rises like a sunrise. She sings, and forty million people go silent. Freed Creatures whoosh down the waterslide into the sea.

"My finale!" howls Maxx. He leaps onto the Gold Rush.

Old Glimmer flicks her tail. A wave tips the Gold Rush over, and Maxx lands in the sea with a splash. His hair collapses into a soggy mop.

You throw him a life ring.

"Biggest Rescue EVER," says Zed. "Live."

Maxx looks at his sister. "I'm sorry, Wren." Gus checks Maxx's pockets. No onion.

A month later, Max feeds a baby possum at a rescue shelter. His volunteer badge says MAX. One X.

"One chance," says Wren.

"One's enough," says Max.

"What did the sea say to the Captain?" asks Mo. "Nothing. It just waved!"

"Three out of ten," says BOLT-9. Mo is thrilled.

Far below, Old Glimmer glows. Beside her glows a second light, very small.

"Statistically," says Tully, "that's a baby."
bands.3:

Beneath the yacht, trapped in a gold net the size of a footy field, Old Glimmer glows a slow, frightened blue.

The Soggy Biscuit creeps closer with its lights off. Behind it bobs a little fleet: every Keeper you have beaten, come to help.

BOLT-9 unlocks a hatch beside the waterslide with his old key. "I rate this yacht two out of ten," he whispers.

Wren leads the way to a door marked 5. "Deck 5," she says. "This is where I found them. This is why I ran."

Inside, the cages go on and on. This time, Wren's hands don't shake. Clawsette scuttles along the rows, snipping every lock.

BOLT-9 plugs his wrist into the stream's control desk. "PASSWORD?" it flashes.

Zed types MAXXISGREAT. Wrong. ILOVEME. Wrong.

Wren types SIRNIBBLES. The screen turns green.

"He hasn't changed it since he was nine," she says.

Upstairs, Maxx spreads his arms. "And now, Vantafam..."

Forty million screens flicker, and BOLT-9's calm face fills them all. "Good evening. I rate tonight's show zero out of ten. Allow me to improve it."

His backup scans of every piece of proof play live: the onion script, the squeaky tapes, the one-carrot ledger, the set photos, the gold Wishlist, four million deleted questions and the blueprints. Last of all comes the uncut footage of Maxx throwing the net himself.

The hearts stop. The comments pour in: "Is it scared?" "Is that a CAGE?"

"Cut the feed!" screams Kaydence.

"I can't!" wails Maxx. "It's live! No edits!"

Kaydence forgets that her own camera is on. "When you sink, your followers are mine," she hisses. Thirty-nine million of her fans hear every word.

Tully's radio crackles. "The Reef Rays are winning," she breathes.

Then Wren walks straight into the shot. "Hi, Max," she says. "It's me."

"Wrennie?" says Maxx.

BOLT-9 beams one last memory onto the giant screen: two children feeding a baby possum in a shoebox. "When I grow up," says little Max, "I'm going to save every animal in the world."

"You promised," says Wren.

For the first time ever, Maxx has no catchphrase.

Everyone looks at you. "Your call, Captain," says Zed.

"Open the net," you say.

You pull the crane lever. The gold net falls away, and Old Glimmer rises out of the sea like a sunrise. She sings, and forty million people go silent. Down the waterslide, a river of freed Creatures whooshes into the Keepers' waiting boats.

"My finale!" howls Maxx. He leaps onto the Gold Rush.

Old Glimmer gives one gentle flick of her tail. A wave tips the Gold Rush over and drops Maxx into the sea with a splash. His silver hair collapses into a soggy mop.

You throw him a life ring.

"Biggest Rescue EVER," says Zed. "Live."

Maxx looks at his sister. "I'm sorry, Wren," he says. Gus checks Maxx's pockets. No onion.

A month later, at a rescue shelter, a young man feeds a baby possum with an eyedropper. His volunteer badge says MAX. One X.

"One chance," says Wren.

"One's enough," says Max.

"What did the sea say to the Captain?" asks Mo that night. "Nothing. It just waved."

"Three out of ten," says BOLT-9. Mo nearly falls overboard with joy.

Far below, Old Glimmer glows. Beside her glows something new: a second light, very small.

"Statistically," says Tully, grinning, "that's a baby."
bands.4:
The Vantadome blazes on the black sea like a floating gold crown. On forty million screens, a countdown glows: "BIGGEST RESCUE EVER, LIVE!"

Beneath the yacht, trapped in a gold net the size of a footy field, Old Glimmer glows a slow, frightened blue. Speakers on deck play her own song back to her, over and over.

"Maxx it out, Vantafam!" cries Maxx, his hair sprayed higher than ever. "Tonight, I rescue THE BIG ONE!"

"Stay cray!" adds Kaydence Kray beside him, her helmet camera blinking.

Out in the dark, the Soggy Biscuit creeps closer with its lights off. Behind it bobs a strange little fleet: a barnacled ship, a tin bathtub, a red umbrella on a raft. Every Keeper you have beaten has come to help.

"Statistically," whispers Tully, "we have a four per cent chance."

"Four is more than none," says Gus.

Indi's final disguise is gold tracksuits made of chocolate wrappers. Mo's says "GOLDIE (MO)".

BOLT-9 unlocks a hatch beside the waterslide with his old key. "Welcome aboard, Captain. I rate this yacht two out of ten."

Wren leads the way through gold corridors until she stops at a door marked 5.

"Deck 5," she says quietly. "This is where I found them. This is why I ran."

Inside, the cages go on and on: hundreds of Creatures from every Island. This time, Wren's hands don't shake. Clawsette scuttles along the rows, snipping every lock.

BOLT-9 plugs his wrist into the stream's control desk. "PASSWORD?" it flashes.

Zed types MAXXISGREAT. Wrong. ILOVEME. Wrong.

Wren reaches past him and types SIRNIBBLES. The screen turns green.

"He hasn't changed it since he was nine," she says.

Upstairs, Maxx spreads his arms. "And now, Vantafam, the moment you've all been waiting for..."

Forty million screens flicker, and BOLT-9's calm face fills them all.

"Good evening, Vantafam. I am BOLT-9, Mr Vantablack's former butler. I rate tonight's show zero out of ten. Allow me to improve it."

His eyes blaze, and his backup scans of every piece of proof he ever dusted play live. The Rescue Script, with its onions. The squeaky tapes: "Squee! You're my hero!" The ledger: four million dollars in, one carrot out. The set photos and their tiny cages. The gold Wishlist, ticked. Four million deleted questions, all popping up at once. The blueprints for a prison with a gift shop. Last of all comes the uncut footage of Maxx throwing the net with his own hands.

The hearts stop. The comments pour in: "Is it scared?" "Is that a CAGE?" "MAXX???"

"Cut the feed!" screams Kaydence.

"I can't!" wails Maxx. "It's live! No edits!"

Kaydence forgets that her own helmet camera is still on. "Keep smiling, Maxxy," she hisses. "When you sink, your followers are mine." Thirty-nine million of her fans hear every word, and her follower count starts falling like snow.

Tully's radio crackles. "The Reef Rays are winning," she breathes.

"TULLY!"

Then Wren walks straight into the shot.

"Hi, Max," she says. "It's me."

Maxx's famous smile slides right off his face. "Wrennie?"

BOLT-9 beams one last memory onto the giant screen: two children feeding a baby possum in a shoebox. "When I grow up," says little Max, "I'm going to save every animal in the world."

"You promised," says Wren.

For the first time ever, Maxx has no catchphrase.

Then everyone looks at you.

"Your call, Captain," says Zed.

"Open the net," you say.

You pull the crane lever, and Clawsette snips the last rope. The gold net falls away, and Old Glimmer rises out of the sea like a sunrise, her glowing wings wider than a footy field. She sings, and forty million people go silent. Down the waterslide, a river of freed Creatures whooshes into the Keepers' waiting boats.

"My finale!" howls Maxx. He leaps onto the Gold Rush and roars after the ray.

Old Glimmer gives one gentle flick of her tail. A wave lifts the Gold Rush, tips it over and drops Maxx into the sea with an enormous splash. His silver wave of hair collapses into a soggy mop.

The crew looks at you again. You throw him a life ring.

"Biggest Rescue EVER," says Zed. "Live."

Dripping on the deck, Maxx looks at his sister. "I'm sorry, Wren," he says. Gus checks Maxx's pockets for an onion. There isn't one.

A month later, at a rescue shelter on Hollowgum Island, a young man in a volunteer shirt feeds a baby possum with an eyedropper. His badge says MAX. One X.

"One chance," says Wren from the doorway.

"One's enough," says Max.

That night, the crew lies on deck under the stars.

"What did the sea say to the Captain?" asks Mo. "Nothing. It just waved."

"Three out of ten," says BOLT-9. Mo nearly falls overboard with joy. "And I rate this whole year ten out of ten. Even the leak."

Gus sneezes. The boat springs a leak. Everyone laughs.

Far below, Old Glimmer glows. Beside her glows something new: a second light, very small.

"Statistically," says Tully, grinning, "that's a baby."
